'''Anna Louise Watts''' is a Professor of Astrophysics at the [[University of Amsterdam]]. She studies [[neutron star]]s and their thermonuclear explosions.<ref name=gs>{{Google scholar id}}</ref><ref name="TurollaZane2015">{{cite journal|last1=Turolla|first1=R|last2=Zane|first2=S|last3=Watts|first3=A L|title=Magnetars: the physics behind observations. A review|journal=Reports on Progress in Physics|volume=78|issue=11|year=2015|article-number=116901|issn=0034-4885|doi=10.1088/0034-4885/78/11/116901|pmid=26473534|arxiv=1507.02924|bibcode=2015RPPh...78k6901T|s2cid=15317167}}</ref>

== Education ==
Watts was educated at [[Bradford Girls' Grammar School]].<ref name="Wijngaarden">{{Cite web|url=https://api-alumni.nl/alumni/alumnus/anna-watts/|title=API - Alumni - Dr. Anna Watts|last=Wijngaarden|first=Evert Rol, Martin Heemskerk, David Hendriks, Timo Halbesma, Marcella|website=api-alumni.nl|language=en|access-date=2018-03-16}}</ref> She studied physics at [[Merton College, Oxford]], and graduated with a first class degree from the [[University of Oxford]] in 1995.<ref name="Woods 2018">{{Cite web|url=https://cdn.southampton.ac.uk/assets/imported/transforms/content-block/UsefulDownloads_Download/18D07A18DA794B919D8F033EECE7054A/anna_watts.pdf|title=Dr Anna Watts|last=Woods|first=Karen|date=|website=University of Southampton|access-date=2018-03-16}}</ref> She entered the science stream at the [[Ministry of Defence (United Kingdom)|Ministry of Defence]] on a graduate scheme, where she worked for five years.<ref name="Woods 2018" /> Watts completed her [[PhD]]<ref name=aphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|first=Anna Louise|last=Watts|year=2003|publisher=University of Southampton|title=The dynamics of differentially rotating neutron stars|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.432636}}|oclc=500094585|url=https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/50593/|website=soton.ac.uk}}</ref> in physics supervised by {{Interlanguage link|Nils Andersson (physicist)|qid=Q57275286}} in the [[general relativity]] group researching neutron stars.<ref name="Woods 2018" /><ref name=page>{{Cite web|url=https://www.southampton.ac.uk/maths/about/our_students/anna_watts.page|title=Anna Watts, Mathematical Sciences |publisher= University of Southampton|website=southampton.ac.uk|language=en|access-date=2018-03-16}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
After her PhD Watts moved to [[Washington, D.C.]] to work as a postdoctoral fellow at [[Goddard Space Flight Center]].<ref name=page/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasa.gov/centers/goddard/news/topstory/2006/starquake.html|title=NASA - NASA Sees Hidden Structure of Neutron Star in Starquake|website=nasa.gov|language=en|access-date=2018-03-16}}</ref> She then received a fellowship at the [[Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics]] in Munich.<ref name=page/><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wwwmpa.mpa-garching.mpg.de/mpa/research/current_research/hl2006-5/hl2006-5-en-print.html|title=MPA :: Current Research Highlight :: May 2006|website=wwwmpa.mpa-garching.mpg.de|access-date=2018-03-16}}</ref> In 2008 Watts joined the [[Anton Pannekoek Institute for Astronomy]].<ref name="Wijngaarden"/>

Watts looks to understand the physics behind the violent dynamic events that occur on neutron stars. These include magnetic flares, [[thermonuclear explosion]]s, and starquakes.<ref name="Amsterdam 2018">{{Cite web|url=http://www.uva.nl/en/profile/w/a/a.l.watts/a.l.watts.html|title=dr. A.L. (Anna) Watts - University of Amsterdam|last=Amsterdam|first=Universiteit van|website=uva.nl|language=en|access-date=2018-03-16}}</ref> Her research lies at the intersection of [[theoretical physics]] and [[astrophysics]]. Working with Tod Strohmayer she identified the hidden structure of a neutron star; a 1.6&nbsp;km crust made of material so dense a teaspoon would weigh 10 million tonnes.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wwwmpa.mpa-garching.mpg.de/mpa/research/current_research/hl2006-5/hl2006-5-en-print.html|title=MPA :: Current Research Highlight :: May 2006|website=wwwmpa.mpa-garching.mpg.de|access-date=2018-03-16}}</ref> In 2014 she received an ERC Starter Grant worth €1,500,000 to study the physics of neutron star explosions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.uva.nl/en/shared-content/faculteiten/en/faculteit-der-natuurwetenschappen-wiskunde-en-informatica/news/2014/12/erc-starting-grants-awarded-to-faculty-of-science-researchers.html|title=ERC Starting Grants awarded to Faculty of Science researchers - University of Amsterdam|last=Amsterdam|first=Universiteit van|website=uva.nl|language=en|access-date=2018-03-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180317035916/http://www.uva.nl/en/shared-content/faculteiten/en/faculteit-der-natuurwetenschappen-wiskunde-en-informatica/news/2014/12/erc-starting-grants-awarded-to-faculty-of-science-researchers.html|archive-date=2018-03-17}}</ref>

She is involved in the development future high-energy space telescopes.<ref name="Amsterdam 2018" /> Watts is part of the science team for the [[NASA]] probe Strobe-X.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://gammaray.nsstc.nasa.gov/Strobe-X/Team.html|title=The STROBE-X Team|last=|first=|date=|website=nasa.gov|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190826122259/https://gammaray.nsstc.nasa.gov/Strobe-X/Team.html|archive-date=26 August 2019|access-date=2018-03-16}}</ref> For the Chinese-European Enhanced X-ray Timing and Polarimetry mission, she is chair of the Dense Matter Science Working Group.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.isdc.unige.ch/extp/observatory-science-working-group.html|title=WG4 - Observatory Science|website=isdc.unige.ch|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-03-16}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.isdc.unige.ch/extp/dense-matter-working-group.html|title=WG1 - Dense Matter|website=isdc.unige.ch|language=en-gb|access-date=2018-03-16}}</ref> She is also chair of Network 3 for NOVA, the [[Netherlands Research School for Astronomy]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.astronomenclub.nl/conferentie/programme.php|title=72nd Netherlands Astronomy Conference|website=astronomenclub.nl|language=en|access-date=2018-03-16}}</ref> She served on the European Cooperation in Science & Technology committee.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cost.eu/COST_Actions/ca/CA16214?management|title=COST {{!}} The multi-messenger physics and astrophysics of neutron stars - Management Committee|website=cost.eu|language=en|access-date=2018-03-16}}</ref> Watts has contributed to ''[[Times Higher Education]]'' and ''[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]''.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/books/review-astrophysics-for-people-in-a-hurry-neil-degrasse-tyson-w-w-norton|title=Astrophysics for People in a Hurry, by Neil deGrasse Tyson|date=2017-06-08|work=Times Higher Education (THE)|access-date=2018-03-16|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/youre-targeted-sexually-how-female-astronomers-are-being-hounded-out-of-work/|title=For Female Astronomers, Sexual Harassment Is a Constant Nightmare|date=2016-04-07|work=Broadly|access-date=2018-03-16|language=en-us}}</ref>
